ideas.title: Why the Humpback Whale's Song Travels for Miles #Shorts
ideas.concept: Show how a humpback whale uses patterned, low-frequency song to communicate through the ocean over long distances.
ideas.hook: A whale can send a song farther than your eyes can see.
ideas.keyVisual: Real humpback whale underwater and at the surface, followed by a close-up of its blow and a wide ocean shot that sells the scale of the call.

ideas.title: Why the Gecko Walks on Glass Without Glue #Shorts
ideas.concept: Explain how millions of microscopic hairs on a gecko foot create enough contact to grip smooth surfaces without glue or suction.
ideas.hook: This lizard climbs glass without glue, claws, or suction cups.
ideas.keyVisual: Real gecko close-up walking up a glass pane, macro footage of its toes, then a side view showing the animal moving upside down or vertically.

ideas.title: Why the Mountain Goat Climbs Cliffs That Look Vertical #Shorts
ideas.concept: Reveal how split hooves, flexible toes, and grippy hoof pads let mountain goats move across near-vertical rock.
ideas.hook: That cliff looks vertical—this goat sees a staircase.
ideas.keyVisual: Real mountain goat traversing a steep rocky ledge, tight shots of split hooves finding tiny footholds, and a wide view revealing the drop below.
